candidats.description: Paleo-Indian pictographs (~2100 years old) on an upright loose slab of limestone (likely the Ste. Genevieve Limestone, Middle Mississippian) in Kentucky, USA. The dark gray to black figures shown above are prehistoric Indian charcoal drawings on a slab of limestone in Kentucky's Mammoth Cave, the longest cave on Earth. Cave passages are frequently partially to mostly filled with sediments and breakdown. Breakdown refers to relatively large slabs and block of rock that have detached from cave ceilings and walls. candidats.titre: File:Mummy Ledge (Main Cave, Mammoth Cave, Kentucky, USA) 4.jpg
candidats.description: Western Kentucky's Mammoth Cave is the longest known cave on Earth, with 426 mapped miles as of March 2024. Occasionally, prehistoric human bodies are found in the cave. During the 1930s, cave guides discovered the desiccated corpse of an American Indian that had been crushed under a limestone block. This was in the southeastern stretches of Main Cave, the principal trunk passage in the Mammoth Cave Ridge part of the system. candidats.titre: File:Breakdown in a giant canyon passage (Edwards Avenue, Great Onyx Cave, Flint Ridge, Mammoth Cave National Park, Kentucky, USA) (8314205890).jpg
candidats.description: Breakdown in a giant canyon passage in Great Onyx Cave. Great Onyx Cave is located in the northern part of Flint Ridge in Mammoth Cave National Park, Kentucky, USA. It has 8 miles worth of mapped passages. Geologically, Great Onyx Cave is part of the Mammoth Cave System, but it has become erosively separated from it (although an air flow connection with the Mammoth Cave System has been identified).
